strategy.summary: Reproduce the float16-to-datetime64/timedelta64 NaN cast defect (issue #21762, PR #25592) by building NumPy at the buggy commit 7ed8629885e6 with the PR's test diff applied, then running only test_datetime_nat_casting. The test casts float16 arrays that contain NaN followed by a trailing non-NaN element and asserts exact NaT equality. The transition to check is FAIL on the buggy build and PASS on the fixed build. The defect is in the C cast loop HALF_to_@TYPE@ in numpy/_core/src/multiarray/arraytypes.c.src, so a compiled NumPy build is required. Whether the bug manifests on a given machine is platform-dependent and is the main risk.
strategy.test_command: python -m pytest numpy/_core/tests/test_datetime.py -k test_datetime_nat_casting -p no:cacheprovider -W error::RuntimeWarning -q
strategy.reproducing_test: numpy/_core/tests/test_datetime.py::TestDateTime::test_datetime_nat_casting (the PR diff adds hnan = nan.astype(np.half) with nan = np.array([np.nan]*8+[0]), and asserts hnan.astype('M8[ns]') and hnan.astype('timedelta64[ns]') equal the matching NaT arrays with a trailing 0)
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 7ed8629885e6 with the test diff applied, test_datetime_nat_casting FAILS: the float16 assertions produce a mismatch against the expected NaT array (the unadvanced input pointer or the UB-dependent NaN conversion misplaces or corrupts the trailing element), and/or an 'invalid value' RuntimeWarning is raised, which -W error::RuntimeWarning turns into a failure. On the fixed revision (input pointer advanced on every iteration, NaN branch writes NPY_DATETIME_NAT), the same test PASSES with no warning.
strategy.numerical_probe: np.array([np.nan]*8+[0], dtype=np.float16).astype('m8[ns]') should equal an all-NaT array except the last element, which should be 0 (or 1970-01-01 for datetime), with no RuntimeWarning.

input_output_examples.buggy_output: emits an 'invalid value' RuntimeWarning on NumPy main; result is not reliably NaT
input_output_examples.expected_output: all-NaT array; np.isnat(arr).all() is True; no warning

risks: Platform dependence: issue #21762 says the undefined behaviour may only appear on some hardware or compilers. On x86-64 builds, NaN-to-int64 conversion often yields INT64_MIN, which is already NaT, so the buggy build may pass there. A pass on the buggy revision on such a machine does not mean the test is wrong. Reproduction on other architectures (for example aarch64 or a sanitizer build such as UBSan) may be needed to observe the transition.

The -W error::RuntimeWarning flag is a deliberate choice made here to make the 'invalid value' warning observable as a failure. It is not stated in the evidence. Removing it leaves the value check as the only failure path.
The buggy and fixed revisions must each be built from source, because the defect is in compiled C. An installed wheel of a different version will not reproduce the transition.

Python version is not stated in the evidence (null), so use a Python version supported by the NumPy revision's pyproject.toml. pytest and hypothesis have no documented constraint and no era ceiling, so choose the latest versions compatible with that Python and say so when running.
The numerical backend (BLAS) is not relevant to this cast path, but the build may still link against a BLAS, which is not documented in the passages.
The numpy.test() command in the given test_commands runs the whole suite and does not select this test, so it is replaced by a pytest -k selection.

The commit message 'do not dereference increment' suggests the buggy revision may differ from the PR base; confirm the exact buggy commit contains the unadvanced-pointer code before attributing a failure to it.

oracle.reference_source: assert_equal against an explicit NaT array in test_datetime.py
oracle.why: NaT is an exact integer sentinel (minimum int64), so equality is exact and needs no tolerance.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The float16 assertions compare against the expected NaT-with-trailing-0 array. On the buggy revision the cast loop either leaves the input pointer unadvanced on the NaN branch, so the trailing 0 is read from the wrong position and mismatches, or the UB-dependent NaN conversion yields a non-NaT value or an 'invalid value' RuntimeWarning. Either makes the assertion or the -W error filter fail.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With the input pointer advanced on every iteration and NaN inputs written as NPY_DATETIME_NAT, all 8 NaN elements become NaT and the trailing 0 becomes the expected value. No warning is raised and assert_equal succeeds for both M8[ns] and timedelta64[ns].
